executive_summary: The dataset contains 50 passenger records from the Titanic. Survival rates vary significantly by passenger class and sex, with first-class female passengers showing the highest survival probability. Key data quality concerns include missing age values and near-zero cabin coverage.
dataset_overview: The dataset has 50 rows and 12 columns. Features include numerical variables (Age, Fare, SibSp, Parch), categorical variables (Pclass, Sex, Embarked, Survived), text-like identifiers (Name, Ticket, Cabin), and an integer ID (PassengerId). The target variable is Survived (binary classification).
key_findings_and_patterns: Fare shows right-skewed distribution with a small number of high-value outliers. Age has approximately 20% missing values. Pclass and Fare show strong negative monotonic correlation. Female passengers have disproportionately higher survival rates than male passengers.
potential_issues_and_warnings: Age column has significant missingness (~20%) requiring imputation strategy. Cabin column has very high missing rate (>75%) and may not be useful. Name and Ticket columns are high-cardinality identifiers that should be dropped or feature-engineered. Fare contains extreme outliers that may affect linear models.

preprocessing_steps.description: Impute Age using median or KNN imputation grouped by Pclass.
Drop Cabin (too many missing), Name, and Ticket (high cardinality identifiers) before modeling.

feature_engineering_ideas.description: Create a FamilySize feature from SibSp + Parch + 1 to capture family survival patterns.
Extract honorific title from Name column (Mr., Mrs., Miss., etc.) as a categorical feature.

modeling_suggestions.description: Start with Logistic Regression as an interpretable baseline for this binary classification task.
Gradient Boosted Trees (XGBoost, LightGBM) typically perform well on tabular survival data.

pitfall_warnings.description: Ensure no passenger survival information leaks through proxy features during cross-validation.
Verify that train/test splits are stratified on Survived to maintain class distribution.
